chunks.rationale: Start with SettingsModal.tsx: SETTINGS_PANES, PrefRow, then the return. The window is now a two-pane shell (settingsModal + nav + editor) matching Workflows. Every existing control is still mounted; inactive panes use the hidden attribute so data-hooks and tests keep finding them. Shared .modal/.input/.btn stay for Edit Project / Add Project / Web token — only Settings switched to settingsModal. CSS: settings chrome first, then pref/switch, then the btnPrimary token alignment with ThreadView.
risks: hidden panes stay in the DOM, so querySelector and m.text() still see every section. That is intentional for tests, but a future 'unmount inactive pane' cleanup would break them.

save() still writes daily + orch + settle + PR cap together. Clicking Save on Spend also persists Threads' settle draft if it changed. Same as before, now less obvious because the other fields are off-screen.
Git pane still stacks Source Control + PR cap + worktree GC + Vibe Kanban. It is shorter than the old dump but the longest remaining scroll.
btnPrimary now uses --btn-primary-bg (solid blue, white text) instead of blue-soft. That also restyles Edit Project, Add Project, Web token, GC confirm, and Vibe import.

chunks.rationale: settingsModal.test.tsx 'two-pane chrome' is the new contract: nav order, Threads default, Spend click hides Threads without unmounting spend/otel fields. Existing suites (budget, otel, pool, memory, build, source control, GC, vibe) were left asserting on data-hooks and still pass because hidden content remains queryable.
risks: No test asserts that exactly one pane lacks hidden. A regression that shows every pane at once would still pass the existing field tests.
Save-button index tests still depend on DOM order (daily, orch, PR, settle). Inserting another numeric Save would shift orch/settle clicks.

chunks.rationale: No save-path logic changed: blur/Enter/Save still call the same persist helpers. The only behavioural UI change is which pane is visible. ArrowUp/Down in the section nav moves aria-current and focuses the next item.
risks: A save error paints in the editor header (one role=alert) instead of inside the Budget field. If Memory's janitor error is also present there are two alerts; query('[role=alert]') still finds one.
